records.name: Turkmenistan
records.summary_text:
Turkmenistan is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. Male same-sex conduct is criminalised (up to 2 years under Article 135) and, more fundamentally, Turkmenistan is one of the world's most closed states: the state exerts strict media control and heavy internet monitoring, no independent research on LGBTI issues has been possible since 2019, and asylum is the community's most urgent need (ILGA-Europe). Amnesty has documented systematic abuses. There is no legal gender recognition, no community, no recourse, and no visibility — the only safe strategy is total concealment.

records.name: Syria
records.summary_text: Syria is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. Articles 520/517 of the Penal Code criminalise “sexual acts against nature” and public indecency; there is no legal gender recognition. Since the fall of the Assad regime (December 2024), the situation has worsened: the Guardians of Equality Movement documented “waves of violence” against Syrian transgender women in the first two months of 2025, implicating both non-state armed groups and security forces in multiple cities, and February 2025 videos showed authorities arresting trans women. sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Syria
sources.claim_summary: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer (LGBTQ) people in Syria face serious legal challenges which are not experienced by non-LGBTQ residents. Article 520 of the penal code of 1949 prohibits "carnal relations against the order of nature," punishable with a prison sentence
